concepts.name: Abolition of Planning Commission and Establishment of NITI Aayog
key_dimensions: Planning Commission abolished by executive order (not by legislation) — constitutional/legal trap
Date of establishment: January 1, 2015 via Cabinet Resolution
Why abolition was justified: top-down approach, lack of state participation, centralized planning failures
NITI Aayog has NO constitutional backing unlike Finance Commission (Article 280) — a common UPSC trap

concepts.name: NITI Aayog vs Planning Commission: Structural and Functional Differences
key_dimensions: Planning Commission had power to allocate funds; NITI Aayog has NO fund allocation power — most critical distinction
Planning Commission: states were supplicants; NITI Aayog: states are partners (cooperative federalism)
Shift from a 'one size fits all' approach to differentiated, state-specific strategies
UPSC trap: NITI Aayog cannot direct ministries or states — only advisory in nature

concepts.name: Composition and Structure of NITI Aayog
key_dimensions: Chairperson: Prime Minister of India (ex officio)
Governing Council: Chief Ministers of all states + Lt. Governors of UTs — largest body within NITI Aayog
Regional Councils: formed for specific issues, chaired by PM or his nominee — ad hoc in nature
Full-time organizational framework: Vice Chairperson, CEO, full-time members, ex officio members, special invitees — distinguish each role

concepts.name: Vice Chairperson and CEO of NITI Aayog: Roles and Distinction
key_dimensions: Vice Chairperson holds Cabinet Minister rank but is NOT a Cabinet Minister — appointment trap
CEO appointed by PM, holds Secretary-level rank, manages day-to-day operations
Vice Chairperson is the de facto head for policy direction; CEO handles administration
Both are appointed by the Prime Minister — no parliamentary confirmation required

concepts.name: Governing Council of NITI Aayog
key_dimensions: Comprises CMs of all states and Lt. Governors of UTs with legislature — note: UTs without legislature may be excluded or represented differently
Apex body for fostering cooperative federalism
Meetings chaired by the Prime Minister — frequency not fixed by any statute
Governing Council ≠ Inter-State Council (Article 263) — both deal with states but different legal basis and functions

concepts.name: Regional Councils in NITI Aayog
key_dimensions: Constituted to address specific regional issues cutting across state boundaries
Chaired by PM or his nominee — not permanent bodies, convened as needed
Include CMs and Lt. Governors of states/UTs in that region
Key distinction: Regional Councils are ad hoc; Governing Council is permanent — UPSC loves this nuance

concepts.name: Advisory Role and Lack of Statutory/Constitutional Power
key_dimensions: NITI Aayog is an advisory think-tank — its recommendations are NOT binding on states or Centre
Cannot allocate Plan funds — this power now vests with Finance Ministry and Finance Commission
Contrast with Planning Commission which had quasi-judicial power over fund allocation
UPSC trap: NITI Aayog has no enforcement mechanism — purely recommendatory

concepts.name: Three-Year Action Agenda, Seven-Year Strategy, and 15-Year Vision Document
key_dimensions: Replaced the Five-Year Plan model with a three-tier planning framework
15-Year Vision Document (2017–2032): long-term aspirational goals
Seven-Year National Development Strategy (2017–2023): medium-term strategy
Three-Year Action Agenda (2017–2020): short-term implementable actions — UPSC may ask which replaced Five-Year Plans

concepts.name: End of Five-Year Plans and Its Implications
key_dimensions: 12th Five-Year Plan (2012–2017) was the last; no 13th Plan — replaced by NITI Aayog's tiered documents
Shift from central allocation-based planning to outcome-based monitoring
States now prepare their own development plans without needing Centre's approval for funds
Implication for federalism: states gain autonomy but also bear more fiscal responsibility

concepts.name: Cooperative Federalism vs Competitive Federalism in NITI Aayog's Mandate
key_dimensions: Cooperative Federalism: shared governance through Governing Council, joint strategy documents
Competitive Federalism: state ranking indices (e.g., SDG India Index, Ease of Doing Business) to incentivize performance
NITI Aayog explicitly mandated to foster BOTH — distinguishing the two is a frequent MCQ/Mains angle
UPSC trap: Planning Commission promoted cooperative federalism too, but NITI Aayog adds the competitive dimension

concepts.name: NITI Aayog's Role in Monitoring and Evaluation
key_dimensions: Development Monitoring and Evaluation Office (DMEO) functions under NITI Aayog
Replaced the Programme Evaluation Organisation (PEO) of the Planning Commission
Tracks implementation of government schemes and flagship programmes
Publishes outcome-based reports — shifts focus from input-based to outcome-based governance

concepts.name: SDG India Index and Localization of SDGs
key_dimensions: NITI Aayog is the nodal agency for SDG implementation and monitoring in India
SDG India Index ranks states and UTs on 17 SDGs — promotes competitive federalism
Helps identify lagging states for focused interventions (Aspirational Districts overlap)
SDG localization: NITI Aayog works with states to align state plans with SDG targets

concepts.name: Aspirational Districts Programme (ADP)
key_dimensions: Launched 2018; covers 112 most backward districts — convergence of central and state schemes
NITI Aayog provides strategic and technical support; implementation by state governments and district collectors
Five focus areas: Health & Nutrition, Education, Agriculture, Financial Inclusion, Infrastructure
Delta Ranking methodology: ranks districts on incremental improvement, not absolute status — UPSC trap

concepts.name: NITI Aayog as a Think-Tank: Research, Innovation, and Knowledge Hub
key_dimensions: Acts as India's premier policy think-tank providing directional and policy inputs
Atal Innovation Mission (AIM) housed under NITI Aayog — promotes innovation and entrepreneurship
Conducts sectoral studies and working papers on economy, agriculture, health, energy etc.
Knowledge and Innovation Hub: collaborates with international organizations (World Bank, UN agencies)

concepts.name: Atal Innovation Mission (AIM) under NITI Aayog
key_dimensions: Flagship initiative to promote innovation ecosystem — Atal Tinkering Labs (schools) and Atal Incubation Centres
Administered directly by NITI Aayog — not a separate statutory body
Atal Tinkering Labs: STEM-based innovation in schools; Atal Incubation Centres: startup support in institutions
UPSC trap: AIM is under NITI Aayog, not Ministry of Science & Technology or DPIIT

concepts.name: NITI Aayog's Role in Fiscal Federalism (Post-14th Finance Commission Context)
key_dimensions: 14th Finance Commission increased states' share in central taxes from 32% to 42% — reduced need for Plan transfers
This structural change made Planning Commission's role in fund allocation redundant — directly enabled NITI Aayog model
NITI Aayog does NOT recommend tax devolution (that is Finance Commission's role) — critical distinction
UPSC trap: Confusing NITI Aayog with Finance Commission on fiscal transfer recommendations

concepts.name: Special Invitees and Ex Officio Members of NITI Aayog
key_dimensions: Ex Officio members: up to 4 Cabinet Ministers nominated by PM — currently include Finance Minister, Home Minister etc.
Special Invitees: domain experts nominated by PM — neither full members nor ex officio
Full-time members: eminent experts/practitioners appointed by PM for fixed terms
Distinction: Ex officio members hold Cabinet rank by virtue of their Cabinet position, NOT because of NITI membership

concepts.name: NITI Aayog and Centre-State Relations: A Federalism Perspective
key_dimensions: States now have more ownership in policy formulation through Governing Council participation
However, critics argue NITI Aayog is still Centre-dominated since PM chairs all key bodies
Comparison with Inter-State Council (Article 263): ISC is statutory; NITI Aayog is non-statutory
UPSC trap: NITI Aayog strengthening federalism vs Finance Commission — both serve federalism but through different mechanisms

concepts.name: Criticism and Limitations of NITI Aayog
key_dimensions: Lacks fund allocation power — states argue it has reduced bargaining leverage with Centre
Advisory body with no enforcement — recommendations can be ignored by states or ministries
Perceived as a 'toothless' body compared to Planning Commission which had real financial power
Accountability deficit: not accountable to Parliament; no statutory mandate — governance gap argument for Mains

concepts.name: NITI Aayog's Sectoral Indices and Ranking Frameworks
key_dimensions: Health Index, School Education Quality Index, SDG India Index, Innovation Index — all published by NITI Aayog
Purpose: evidence-based policymaking and competitive federalism through peer pressure among states
Export Preparedness Index, Water Management Index — less known but UPSC-relevant
UPSC trap: These indices are NITI Aayog outputs, not Ministry outputs — attribution questions are common in Prelims
